records: Ian, take this over, will you?
The barkeep gives Ian a routine serving task before the customers' attention becomes intrusive.
Yes.
Keep Ian's brief, polite acknowledgment while working.
That's him. Isn't he beautiful...?
The woman admires Ian; do not invent a prior romance, marriage or familiarity with him.
Is that really a man?
Preserve the male customer's incredulous remark as his own reaction, not a change to Ian's identity.
Shh! He'll hear you.
The woman hushes her companion; the paired role labels alone do not establish marriage.
(Not again... Give it a rest. I'm not here to be gawked at...)
Preserve Ian's internal frustration at repeated objectification; parentheses distinguish thought from spoken dialogue.
Ian, take these drinks over, too.
Keep the barkeep's next serving request without specifying an unbound type of alcohol.
...Yes.
The pause maintains Ian's subdued response after the unwanted attention.
Oh! Ian himself brought our drinks!
The woman's delight concerns being served by Ian; omit the Japanese honorific without inventing a relationship.
What's so exciting about that? Tch. This is no fun.
Her companion reacts with irritation and jealousy; do not turn him into a named husband.
Ian. Hey, take this to that table.
Retain the barkeep's repeated direction and concrete table destination.
Yes.
Keep Ian's professional acknowledgment before the patron addresses him.
Hey, sweetheart. Pour me a drink, would you? Heh heh.
The patron's feminizing catcall is intentional harassment, not a family address or a statement of Ian's gender.
Ian initially refuses to engage with the catcall.
You really are a pretty thing, aren't you? Hmm?
Preserve the patron's insistent, objectifying attention rather than recasting it as welcome praise.
The second silence sustains Ian's resistance to the patron's escalating behavior.
Are you really a man? With skin that fair? Heh heh heh...
Unlike Angelo's gloomy-demeanor remark, this source explicitly mentions pale skin; retain the harasser's insinuation without endorsing it or adding an identity claim.
Don't touch me!
Preserve Ian's clear refusal of unwanted physical contact and his agency.
Whoa! Ow, ow, ow!
Keep the patron's pain reaction; no specific wound, stabbing or broken bone is established here.
You bastard!
The patron answers Ian's resistance with an angry insult.
(Damn...!)
Ian's internal realization concerns the trouble his reaction will cause, not regret for having a boundary.
You... That's a fine way to treat a paying customer!
Keep the patron's sarcastic appeal to customer status as his own grievance.
...My apologies.
Ian gives a restrained formal apology under workplace pressure; do not make the harassment welcome.
Barkeep, a drink.
Hodram addresses the proprietor by occupation; 親父 does not imply a father or other family relationship.
Yes, yes, coming right up. ...Ian, a word?
The barkeep shifts from serving Hodram to taking Ian aside.
Ian... I don't think this line of work suits you.
Keep the barkeep's hesitant judgment as the lead-in to dismissal.
But...
Ian begins an unfinished appeal to his employer; avoid translating 親父さん as Dad or inventing a personal name.
I've had enough trouble. There are ways to deal with customers without using a sword.
Preserve the employer's explicit complaint about sword use without retroactively inventing a particular injury.
I'm sorry, but I'll have to let you go.
Make the dismissal clear while preserving the barkeep's regretful delivery.
...I understand.
Ian accepts the dismissal quietly rather than arguing or celebrating.
The way he moved... He's trained with a sword. Quite skilled, too. I should speak to him.
Hodram infers trained swordsmanship from Ian's movement; do not add a military history or school.
(Fired... And no money. What am I going to do...?)
Preserve Ian's concrete financial predicament and uncertainty after losing the job.
(A ship out at sea... I wish I could go back.)
Ian's longing to return to seafaring foreshadows his existing profession without naming a particular former ship.
Well, well, sweetheart! We keep running into each other today.
The same patron resumes the feminizing harassment; this is a threatening recurrence, not a friendly reunion.
Retain Ian's immediate recognition and alarm.
Heh heh... All alone out here? Bad luck for you. Boys!
The patron summons his group and exploits Ian's isolation; do not invent a gang name or exact headcount.
Ian remains silent as the group closes in.
You're not getting away. You made a fool of me back there!
Preserve the patron's retaliation motive and threat, without treating his complaint as justified.
(Too many... I can't take them all. I'll go for the one who looks like the leader!)
Retain Ian's tactical assessment and uncertain identification of the leader, not a guaranteed victory.
What's taking you idiots so long? He's one man! Get on with it!
The leader berates the group for failing to overpower a single opponent.
Heh heh... Pretty face, but you can fight. Watching you struggle is quite a turn-on.
Keep the subordinate's explicit sexualization of the fight and threatening intent; do not sanitize it into admiration or invent a sexual identity.
Hah... Hah... (I can't even get near him on my own...!)
Ian is tiring and cannot reach the intended leader alone; preserve the internal thought separately from his breathing.
Looks like he's about finished... Hurry up and take him out!
Retain the leader's order and mounting danger without specifying an unsupported method of attack.
What...? Who's there!?
The interrupted attack draws the leader's startled reaction to the rescuer.
Grown men ganging up on one opponent... Not very impressive.
Hodram condemns reliance on numbers with controlled disdain; add no new arrest or legal authority.
Damn it... I only pick fights I can win. You'll pay for this!
Preserve the bully's self-serving principle and retreating threat; do not invent a future encounter.
Ian's pause allows the danger to subside before Hodram's awkward observation.
No wonder the women in the tavern were making such a fuss.
Keep Hodram's appearance-related remark after the rescue; its awkwardness prompts Ian's response.
...What I look like... It doesn't matter.
Ian dismisses the importance of his appearance after being objectified; do not recast this as a confession about identity.
Well, you're entitled to your opinion.
Preserve Hodram's dry response without making it a threat or an argument about Ian's gender.
No, I was talking to myself. ...I'm sorry. Thank you. You saved my life.
Ian clarifies the aside, apologizes and sincerely thanks the rescuing party; keep the explicit life-saving gratitude.
No need to thank us. In fact, I have a favor to ask. It's that swordsmanship of yours.
Hodram turns the rescue into a recruitment approach based on Ian's demonstrated skill, not his appearance.
If it's something I can do...
Ian offers help cautiously before knowing the request.
You fought brilliantly back there. How would you like to test that skill out in the world?
Preserve the invitation to broaden the use of his swordsmanship, without inventing a tournament or promised rank.
...? What do you mean?
Ian asks Hodram to explain the figurative invitation.
I'd like you aboard my ship.
Keep the direct shipboard invitation without assigning a particular station.
Do you really mean that? If so, I'd gladly accept, but...
Ian's surprised acceptance remains tentative long enough for Hodram to question it.
What do you mean? Do you think I'm joking?
Hodram mistakes Ian's astonishment for doubt about his sincerity.
No, it's just... The timing couldn't be better.
Ian explains that the opportunity is remarkably timely, not that he distrusted Hodram.
Keep Hodram's brief questioning beat before the final explanation.
I'm a seafarer, currently out of work. I'd be very grateful for a place aboard your ship. My name is Ian Dukov.
航海士 identifies his seafaring profession here, not an assigned navigation station; retain the established full name and eager, polite acceptance.
